Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T)"
- Document: "Larsen & Toubro Limited (L&T) Petrol Dispensing Pumps & Systems"

The document value appears to be the applicant name with a description of the product/scope glued into it: "Petrol Dispensing Pumps & Systems" is clearly a product description, not part of the company name. This looks like an extraction artifact where the product description got concatenated with the company name.

However, the rules say: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

But this isn't a genuinely different company — "Larsen & Toubro Ltd" vs "Larsen & Toubro Limited" is legal-suffix drift (same-entity), and "Petrol Dispensing Pumps & Systems" is an extraction artifact (product description glued into the name).

Per rules: "Extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into a name, obvious OCR noise) = document-noise with best_value from the register."

So the verdict should be "document-noise" with best_value from the register: "Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T)".

Wait — but is "Petrol Dispensing Pumps & Systems" actually part of the official applicant designation? In OIML certificates, sometimes the applicant is listed with a product line. But the rule explicitly says "address fragments glued into a name" = document-noise. A product category glued into a name fits the same pattern — extraction artifact.

Also the applicant in the register "Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T)" matches the embedded comment in the document context: "<!-- applicant: Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T) -->" — interesting, the document's own metadata comment says the same as the register. The "document" value in the conflict presumably comes from the certificate's rendered text.

So verdict: document-noise, best_value = "Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T)".

Why: The document's value is the same company with a product description ("Petrol Dispensing Pumps & Systems") glued on — an extraction artifact; "Ltd" vs "Limited" is legal-suffix drift.
